# `submissions/`

One `<team>_v<N>.parquet` per submission, each with a `.meta.json` sidecar
written by `submit.py` recording exactly which run produced it.

**The index is [`submissions.csv`](submissions.csv)** — generated by
`build_submission_index.py` from those sidecars, joined to the review tier in
`../pipeline_catalog.csv`. Regenerate it after every new submission:

```bash
python build_submission_index.py
```

## Renamed 2026-09-08: `PLACEHOLDER_TEAM_*` → `fearless_barn_*`

`submit.py --team` was a required free-text argument with no default, so every
submission up to v13 was typed by hand as `PLACEHOLDER_TEAM` and 12 files were
built under that placeholder name. The competition contract keys the file on the
registered team name (`<team>_v<N>.parquet`), so this was not cosmetic.

All 13 files were renamed and the `team` field inside each `.meta.json` updated.
The team name now lives in `config.TEAM` and `submit.py --team` defaults to it,
so it cannot be mistyped again.

**Plan documents in `../plans/` (05–13) still reference the old
`PLACEHOLDER_TEAM_v*.parquet` paths.** Those are historical records of past
rounds and have deliberately not been rewritten — the links are stale, the
filenames map one-to-one by version number.

> If any of v1–v12 were actually uploaded under the placeholder name, the
> leaderboard's copy still carries that name; only the local files changed.

## What the index shows

Two warnings print on every regeneration, and both are real:

- **9 of 13 submissions came from arms now quarantined as over-tuned**
  (v4–v6, and v7–v12 which are all `airport_debiased_multimodel`). They are
  marked `reproducible=NO`: those arms are out of `config.ARMS`, and `submit.py`
  takes `--arm` from that list, so the current code cannot rebuild them.
- **Those same 9 skipped the full-period refit** — trained on the `forward`
  split's 8 months (1,387,105 rows) when `full`'s 12 months (2,084,659 rows)
  were available. The build's design is *select on `forward`, refit on `full`,
  submit*; `full` is in `config.SELECTION_FORBIDDEN_SPLITS` precisely so nothing
  can be chosen on it.

**v13 is the first submission since v3 built from a tier-A arm, and the first
ever from `airport_operator_multimodel`** — which could not be submitted at all
until `submit.py`'s `predict_ranking()` dispatch got the branch it was missing.

## Uploading

`submit.py` never uploads. It prints the `mc` command and leaves sending a file
as an explicit human action, so a half-finished model cannot burn a submission
slot by accident. Credentials live in `../../credentials.json` (git-ignored).
